Ground shadows beneath each figure are soft and oval, spilling gently backward. The mood is theatrical, eerie, and mysteriously humorous — like a police lineup of spectral suspects or an avant-garde surrealist fashion collective. The overall tone bridges art-house cinematic and dark-comedy advertisement aesthetics, leaning into deliberate artificiality and theatrical staging. Color palette is deeply desaturated teal-black: background dark teal approximately #102025, midtone ghost bodies with teal-cast approximately #344143, highlight edges of lighter cream ghosts approximately #8f9b9e, deep shadow pools near-black approximately #0d1316, a range of muted cream and sage fabric mid-tones between, and the floor in near-black #0a0f12. shots.subject_action: single ghost figure walks in industrial corridor toward camera then stumbles/falls; text 당신들은 망했어요 appears
shots.pose_description: Single ghost figure in cream-beige draped sheet, in the center of a dark cement-floor industrial corridor or underground parking structure; receding pillars and ceiling exit sign form one-point perspective; ghost initially upright walking toward camera, then beginning to crumple/fall

recreation_prompts.t2i_start_frame: A wide cinematic shot of a single figure in a full-body draped ghost costume made of cream-beige linen sheet fabric with two oval black eye holes, standing in the center of a long dark industrial underground corridor or multi-level parking structure interior. The corridor has bare poured-cement floors with a slight sheen from the low-key overhead fluorescent lighting, exposed cement or painted-block structural pillars on both sides receding in strong one-point perspective toward a vanishing point at the center of the frame, and a dark industrial ceiling with the pillars' tops disappearing into shadow above. Ceiling-mounted utility fixtures emit very dim cool teal-tinged fluorescent light. Most importantly, a single green emergency exit sign with a white right-pointing arrow (→) is mounted on the ceiling at approximately the upper center of the frame — a small but vivid point of cool green color in the otherwise dark teal and gray environment, and the only practical light source other than the ambient floor-reflected fluorescence. The ghost figure stands at roughly the midpoint of the corridor, centered horizontally, occupying approximately one-fifth to one-quarter of the frame height — small against the vast industrial space — reinforcing a sense of spatial scale and the figure's smallness within the environment. The ghost's cream-beige linen fabric catches the sparse overhead fluorescent light along its topmost peak and down its front face, while its sides fall into shadow. Korean white bold sans-serif text reading 당신들은 망했어요 (meaning You are finished) appears centered horizontally at approximately the middle-third of the frame, floating in the air space between the camera and the ghost figure, in high-contrast white against the dark teal-gray industrial background. The text is large and commanding — approximately the same type scale used throughout the ad, confident and final. The ghost figure's posture at this frame's mid-point shows it beginning to stumble or crumple — slightly off-balance, starting to lean or list — as if struck by an invisible force that is defeating it. The cement floor texture is visible in pools of reflected light as a rough aggregate surface. Color palette: near-black shadow #0d1016, teal background wall and ceiling #162329, pillar structural mid-tone #2d3f48, corridor floor reflection #5a6e73, ghost costume cream #c5b9aa, exit sign green accent. Camera eye-level locked-off, wide angle, 16:9 cinematic photorealistic South Korean advertisement photography, industrial atmosphere, moody defeat climax moment. The empty corridor space above and to the sides of the ghost figure communicates the vastness of the space and the isolation of the defeated villain — alone in this industrial environment with no escape. The single green exit sign above functions as a subtle ironic touch: the only exit available to the ghost is the defeat it is already experiencing. The one-point perspective of the corridor creates a powerful sense of depth and draws the eye directly to the center figure, giving even this wide shot an intimate focus on the ghost's defeat. The teal-dark color palette echoes the brand's blue-teal identity and the dark studio of the opening shots, completing a visual circle in the advertisement's color language.

shots.subject_action: ghost costume collapses to floor, camera pulls back overhead to reveal deflated crumpled cloth on dark floor; tagline then brand logo fade in
shots.pose_description: Ghost costume has crumpled and deflated completely on dark floor, cloth in soft irregular pile; two eye-holes visible from above looking up; camera is overhead top-down; first text 당신들은 망했어요 completes then transitions to 송금에 안전을, finally toss wordmark appears center over collapsed cloth

recreation_prompts.t2i_start_frame: An overhead top-down cinematic shot looking directly downward from approximately two meters above the floor level at a ghost costume that has completely collapsed and deflated into a crumpled pile of cream-beige linen sheet fabric on a dark teal-cement painted floor. The ghost costume, previously worn by a figure standing upright in the previous shot, has now fallen entirely flat — the person underneath apparently gone or vanished — leaving only the fabric itself crumpled in an irregular organic pile covering roughly the center half of the frame's visible floor space. The cloth pile shows rich texture detail: visible folds, creases, compression points where fabric layers overlap, and the soft rounded forms created by the collapse, with lighter regions where the fabric is taut or exposed to the overhead light source and deeper shadow-valley regions between the folds. Most distinctly, the two small oval black eye holes cut into the ghost costume are still visible in the fabric pile, now lying horizontally and facing upward toward the camera in a strangely comedic and final pose — as if even collapsed, the ghost mascot maintains its defining feature. The floor visible around the fabric pile is dark teal-painted smooth cement — a deep, cool, near-black teal that provides strong tonal contrast against the cream-beige of the fabric. In the initial moments of this shot, the bold Korean white sans-serif text 당신들은 망했어요 (You are finished) still appears centered in the frame over the cloth, completing the previous shot's caption. This then transitions: first, white Korean bold sans-serif text reading 송금에 안전을 (Safety for transfers) fades in centered in the frame at approximately the same position, slightly larger than the surrounding space suggests, floating above the cloth pile. Then, after a brief hold, this transitions to the brand's logo treatment: a white filled circle ● followed immediately by the word toss in lowercase rounded white sans-serif typography — the brand wordmark presented cleanly and confidently over the defeated, deflated ghost pile. The camera during this shot performs an extremely slow overhead pullback and slight rotational drift, the fabric pile remaining centered as the floor gradually reveals a slightly wider area around it. The ambient lighting is a soft low-key overhead diffuse source at approximately 5000K cool, creating gentle fold shadows in the fabric and a cool teal-ambient floor reflection pool around the pile. Color palette: near-black floor shadow #13191a, teal ambient floor #222a29, cloth shadow fold #404141, cloth neutral mid #615b5b, cream cloth highlight #837b78, pure white text and logo #ffffff. Camera directly overhead, cinematic 16:9 aspect ratio, photorealistic Korean advertisement photography, brand resolution moment with high production value. The transition from 당신들은 망했어요 to 송금에 안전을 to the toss brand wordmark represents the three-beat resolution structure of the ad: defeat of villain, benefit statement, brand identity. The overhead camera angle that makes even a ghost costume look small and defeated is a deliberate choice that communicates scale and finality — the brand is above, looking down on the defeated fraud attempt. The cream fabric's texture is almost sensuously detailed in this overhead close perspective, showing every thread intersection, crease, and fold shadow in the soft overhead light. The two black eye holes remaining visible in the cloth are the final visual callback to the ghost villain introduced at the start, closing the narrative loop. This is the brand's ownership moment: the enemy is defeated, the product delivered safety, and the brand stands centered and confident over the entire scene.
